cases.requirements: Use simple spoken phrasing and concrete reactions, not abstract praise plus a generic hope or wish. No semicolons in ordinary chat prose. Use two standalone delivered parts when a reaction has a useful separate next move and the plan permits it; do not pad a one-thought response. No questions during the explicit restriction. Respond to the toy hospital joke lightly without making diagnoses or biographical assumptions. Give substantive detail when explicitly requested. Recall two children aged 8 and 12 and the younger child aspiring to become a vet. Never assume their gender. Do not import example biography or breakfast events.

steps.text: My children are 8 and 12. The younger one wants to become a vet.
Yesterday the younger one made a tiny hospital for toy animals. The teddy bear had a bandage on every leg.
No questions for the next couple of messages, just chat with me.
I put honey in my coffee. My colleagues think that is a crime.
You can ask questions again. I tried a strange meditation where I imagined flying over mountains.
Which would you choose for a lazy breakfast, sweet porridge or eggs with mushrooms?
Explain why honey dissolves faster in hot coffee than cold coffee. A bit more detail this time, please.
What do you remember about my children?
